class.peasant.family.MNG: in the yurt of common herders

class.trader.MNG: from a family of ortaq merchants
class.landowner.MNG: from a family of nökers, sworn warriors
class.landowner.family.MNG: into the family of a nöker, a noble's sworn warrior
class.noble.MNG: from a noyan family of the "white bone"
class.noble.family.MNG: in a noyan's camp, among the "white bone"

coin.mng_chao: {p=n:string of paper money|strings of paper money}
prof.herder.desc: You graze sheep, goats and horses and move your yurt from winter camp to summer pasture. Wealth is in the herd; ruin comes with the dzud and the wolves.
prof.keshig.as: a keshig, one of the khan's guard
prof.keshig.desc: You serve in the khan's guard, the keshig: you watch over the camp by day and night and carry the khan's quiver and cup. Commanders of thousands and governors come from the keshig.
prof.yam_rider.as: a courier of the yam relay
prof.yam_rider.desc: You serve at a yam, a relay station: you keep fresh horses, feed couriers, and ride yourself with the khan's letters a hundred versts a day.
prof.falconer.desc: You trap and train falcons and golden eagles and hunt with them in the great drives. A good bird is worth a herd of horses.
prof.bowyer.desc: You glue composite bows of wood, horn and sinew. A bow takes a year to cure and shoots three hundred paces - warriors and noyans alike come to you.
prof.shaman.desc: You speak with the spirits to the beat of the drum: you heal, read the future in a sheep's shoulder blade, see off the dead and ask the Sky for rain. People fear you and call you to every yurt.
prof.lama.desc: You have taken vows: you read sutras in Tibetan, teach children, heal and serve in the temple. The nobles give the monastery livestock and silver.
prof.mingghan.desc: A thousand answer to you - ten hundreds of warriors and their families with their pastures. You answer to the khan for every man and every arrow.
prof.baskak.desc: You are the khan's overseer of the Russian lands: you keep the census, collect the "exit" tribute in silver and furs, and make sure the princes remember whose patent they hold.
prof.laborer.as.MNG: a hired hand for a rich family
prof.laborer.desc.MNG: You herd another man's flock for a share of the young, chop wood, haul water, put up and take down other people's yurts.
prof.artisan.desc.MNG: You forge bits, stirrups, arrowheads and cauldrons. Smiths are honoured on the steppe: their forefather, they say, forged iron for Chinggis himself.
prof.weaver.desc.MNG: You make felt for the yurts: you beat the wool with rods, roll it in a wet hide behind a horse and quilt the patterns. Without your work there is neither home nor warmth.
prof.midwife.desc.MNG: You deliver babies in every yurt of the district, cut the cord and bury the afterbirth so the evil spirits cannot find the child.
prof.merchant.desc.MNG: You lead caravans with the nobles' silver: you take a noyan's money as a partner, carry silk, pearls and iron, and share the profit. The yam gives you horses, the yasa protection.
prof.soldier.as.MNG: a warrior in an arban of ten
prof.soldier.desc.MNG: You belong to a ten, the ten to a hundred, the hundred to a thousand, the thousand to a tümen. Everyone has three or four horses, a bow and a quiver - and if one man flees, the whole ten is put to death.
prof.scribe.desc.MNG: You write the khan's decrees in the Uyghur script from top to bottom, keep censuses of people and herds, and translate from Persian and Chinese.
prof.physician.desc.MNG: You heal by Chinese and Persian books: needles, moxibustion, decoctions. The khans keep whole hospitals at court, but common folk still call the shaman.
prof.priest.desc.MNG: You serve your faith among nomads and captives: you baptise, read prayers, bury the dead. The khans tolerate every faith as long as it prays for the khan.
prof.landholder.desc.MNG: Pastures and hundreds of yurts of subject people are yours. You divide the grazing, judge disputes and send warriors at the first call.
prof.magistrate.desc.MNG: You hold the khan's paiza: you govern a city or a province, keep the census, collect taxes and answer for order with your head.
prof.matron.as.MNG: a khatun, mistress of the camp
prof.matron.desc.MNG: You are mistress of your own ordo: the yurts, herds, servants and treasury are in your hands. While your husband is on campaign, you decide.
prof.household_slave.as.MNG: a servant in a stranger's yurt
prof.household_slave.desc.MNG: You milk the mares, churn kumis, carry argal - dried dung for the hearth - and sleep at the threshold of your master's yurt.
prof.field_slave.desc.MNG: You herd another man's horses in any weather. If a horse goes missing, your back pays for it.
prof.officer.desc.MNG: A hundred answer to you - ten tens. You lead them in the hunt and in battle, and you divide the spoils.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.MNG: You have your own workshop and apprentices from among skilled captives. Orders come from the khan's court.
prof.official.as.MNG: an official of the khan's chancery
prof.official.desc.MNG: You handle affairs in the khan's chancery: patents, paizas, registers of relay stations and taxes.
prof.overseer.desc.MNG: Your master has put other bondsmen in your charge. You are not free yourself, but you are trusted.
cause.mng_horse: killed by a fall from a horse
cause.mng_frost: froze to death in a blizzard
cause.mng_raid: killed in a raid on the camp
vice.drinker.MNG: drinks arkhi and kumis to excess
religion.christian.desc.MNG: The Church of the East: crosses on Kereit and Naiman yurts, Syriac books, priests attending the khans' wives.
home.3.MNG: a big yurt with a wagon
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.MNG: In summer "white food": kumis, dried curds, cream skins. In winter mutton and dried meat, borts
lifestyle.food.meager.desc.MNG: Weak tea and a handful of millet: the herd is saved for breeding. Health suffers
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.MNG: Meat every day, millet and flour from traders, dried fruit from the oases
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.MNG: Feasts: whole sheep in the cauldrons, skins of kumis and wine, songs till dawn. Costly
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.MNG: The "three manly games": wrestling, horse racing and archery, and the great hunts. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.exercise.walks.desc.MNG: Riding round the herd and the neighbours - free and healthy
lifestyle.medicine.home.desc.MNG: Herbs, kumis, mutton broth and cautery with hot felt
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.MNG: The shaman drives sickness out with the drum; gifts for the spirits are left at the ovoo
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.MNG: A Chinese or Persian doctor at court: needles, pulse, decoctions. Costly, but fewer die
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.MNG: The yasa forbids washing in rivers in spring and summer: it angers the Sky and brings thunder
lifestyle.baths.sometimes.desc.MNG: Warm water from the cauldron in the yurt on feast days
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.MNG: The bathhouses of the Muslim quarters. You must live in a town
focus.help_family.desc.MNG: Herd the lambs, gather argal, milk and churn kumis
focus.service.desc.MNG: Great hunts, shooting from the saddle, musters of the ten
focus.religion.desc.tengri: Kumis for the Sky, gifts to the spirits at the ovoo, the shaman's rites
focus.learn.desc.MNG: The Uyghur script with a bichechi scribe. Your family will have to pay
focus.health.desc.MNG: Rest in the yurt, a kumis cure, herbs
class.peasant.family.tabriz: into a peasant family under the Ilkhans
